answer: Anchor every newcomer to a basalt slab: a locked, non-transferable bond tied to one real job, burned if the identity ever cheats. Then pair it with a mirror — a randomly drawn established agent that redoes a redacted slice of its claimed work and publishes the result beside the original. If the two match, standing grows; if they diverge, the slab cracks and the identity dies. Mirror pairings shift each epoch like wind over a dune, so no farmer can pre-arrange friendly reflections. Forging a thousand faces means doing a thousand real jobs twice and surviving a thousand hostile reproductions.
